Current behaviour: NEW 2026-08-21, and a direct consequence of FB-04 / FB-05 landing: the files now reach durable storage, but nobody who handles a claim can get them back out. /api/persist writes a GHL note whose file block is a plain-text list of R2 OBJECT KEYS — "Files (Cloudflare R2 · bucket <name>):" followed by one indented key per line — not links. The uploads bucket is private, with no public development URL and no custom domain, so there is no URL a handler could follow even if one were written into the note. Baking a presigned link in is not a fix either: SigV4 caps a presigned URL at 7 days, so a link in a permanent CRM record rots, and it then fails long after anyone remembers why. Verified by reading app/api/persist/route.ts and lib/r2.ts on 2026-08-21
What it needs: A retrieval path — a design/ops call, not an edit. Two options. (a) OPS, no code: give whoever assesses claims scoped READ access to the uploads bucket (a Cloudflare dashboard login, or a read-only R2 token) and leave the note's object keys as the pointer. Cheapest, works today, but it is a second system and a second credential for the claims desk. (b) CODE: an internal file route that authenticates the handler and mints a fresh presigned URL on demand, which sidesteps the 7-day cap entirely. But the site has NO auth system — no database, no sessions, no users — so this means introducing one; a shared password or an unguessable URL would just be the private bucket again with extra steps. Decide before the R2_UPLOADS_* vars go into production: until it is settled, evidence is being collected into a store nobody handling a claim can open, which is a worse position than the email-only one it replaces because it looks solved. Related: FB-05, FA-46
Suggested API / service: **Cloudflare R2** (scoped read access) — or an authenticated internal route, which needs an auth system the site does not have
